candidates.claim: sw-core-01 has a global 'username vendor2' line that was added relative to the approved baseline.
candidates.remediation: Reconcile against the approved baseline: confirm that the vendor2 account is authorized and documented, or remove it.

candidates.claim: Non-OT-facing trunk ports (sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 and Gi1/0/24, sw-ot-01 Gi1/0/24 uplink) allow VLAN 10, while the registry says only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10.

rtr-01 has a management-side interface (GigabitEthernet0, 10.10.99.12/24) with no ACL and a default route via the OUTSIDE next hop 198.51.100.1, and the only bound ACL (EDGE_IN) filters inbound traffic on Gi0/0/0 only, so MGMT traffic reaching rtr-01 could be forwarded to OUTSIDE outside the approved services.

clarifications.question: The approved trunk list allows VLAN 10 on sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 and Gi1/0/24 and on the sw-ot-01 Gi1/0/24 uplink, but the registry also says only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10. Should these trunks be treated as approved exceptions, or as violations of the VLAN 10 rule?

rtr-01 GigabitEthernet0 (10.10.99.12/24) sits in MGMT with no ACL, and rtr-01 has two default routes, one via the OUTSIDE next hop 198.51.100.1 and one via the fw-01 mgmt address 10.10.99.1. Is this intentional? If MGMT hosts can reach rtr-01 and be forwarded to OUTSIDE, that bypasses the MGMT_IN policy on fw-01 and the approved-services rule.
